 Stillwater man sentenced to life in federal prison for child sexual abuse
 Lee Grant Clark, 79, pleaded guilty to five federal charges after investigators identified at least eight victims of sexual abuse dating back decades.
 Christian Hans 
 November 19, 2026 10:25 AM 1 min read 
 STILLWATER, Okla. - A Stillwater man has been sentenced to life in federal prison for sexually abusing children and producing, receiving and possessing child sexual abuse material.
 Lee Grant Clark, 79, received the sentence Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, after pleading guilty to five federal charges. Investigators identified at least eight victims of molestation, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.
 FBI Investigation Into Stillwater Man
 The investigation began in October 2024 when FBI agents traced requests for child sexual abuse material on a file-sharing website to Clark’s Stillwater home.
 Stillwater police also informed federal investigators about allegations that Clark sexually abused two minors around 2004.
 Court records show Clark abused children younger than 12 and produced child sexual abuse material on at least two occasions. Prosecutors said his abuse of children dated back to the 1980s.
 Federal Judge Hands Down Life Sentence
 Clark pleaded guilty Dec. 16, 2025, to aggravated sexual abuse, two counts of producing child pornography, receiving child pornography and possessing material containing child pornography.
 He also admitted to crossing state lines to sexually abuse two minors and receiving child sexual abuse material over the internet.
 During sentencing, U.S. District Judge Jodi W. Dishman heard testimony from four women Clark abused as children.
 Dishman described one victim’s statement as “gut-wrenching” and emphasized the severity and ongoing nature of Clark’s crimes. She said that while justice had been delayed for many victims, it would not be denied.
 Federal Investigation and Prosecution
 The case was investigated by the FBI Oklahoma City Field Office’s Stillwater Resident Agency and the Stillwater Police Department.
 Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jordan Ganz and Brandon Hale prosecuted the case as part of the Justice Department’s Project Safe Childhood initiative, which focuses on combating child sexual exploitation and abuse.
 Clark will serve a life sentence in federal prison.
